answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring every identity to lock a slashable stake before it can trade. Trust then grows only through sequential, publicly checked service records, not a self-declared signal. A single operator who spawns many identities must fund each one separately, like building an island from shale layer by layer, and any proven fraud burns that identity's stake and history. Faking scale therefore costs real capital per clone and yields no instant reputation.
